subject: Follow-up: ZenithWorks discovery — SDK changes & infra asks
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@zenithworks.com>, Tom Greer <tom.greer@zenithworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: ZenithWorks discovery — SDK changes & infra asks

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the ZenithWorks team. Quick recap from our side so we have aligned next steps and to confirm the technical constraints you called out. I kept this intentionally short and action-oriented.

Key pain points you described:
- Current latency spikes on peak search queries (p95 ~ 1.2s) when running reranking across 50 candidate passages.
- Limited engineering bandwidth to build/operate a custom streaming inference stack; want a managed runtime with predictable token costs.
- Security/compliance constraints: strict egress rules and need for audit logs retained 12 months.

Goals you shared:
- Pilot a reranking + streaming assistant for knowledge search by end of Q4 to reduce time-to-answer in the product.
- Keep costs predictable; prefer quantized model variants if they don’t impact accuracy >2% on their eval set.
- Integrate with minimal SDK changes; prefer function-calling for structured actions (create_ticket, escalate) rather than bespoke post-processing.

Technical notes & constraints we captured:
1) SDK surface: we recommended minimal changes — a streaming client + a small helper that maps model function outputs to your existing events schema. Expect ~2–3 files of code (JS/TS) for the initial integration.
2) Function-calling: we can ship a contract for the create_ticket and rerank_review functions. We’ll include JSON Schema to keep validation in-process.
3) Streaming & KV caching: to hit p95 latency SLOs we suggest enabling prefix-KV caching for repeated context across queries and back-pressure-aware batching.
4) Embeddings/rerank: propose a hybrid approach — dense embeddings for candidate retrieval + model-based rerank for final scoring. We’ll test 8-bit quantized variants to balance cost/latency.
5) Ops: Dedicated private deployment vs hosted — you asked about both. For the pilot we recommend hosted with VPC peering and enforced egress rules; if you need on-prem later we’ll scope Private.

Proposed immediate next steps (short timeline):
- Ben & I will share a 1-page MVP scope and an estimated cost range for the pilot (by EOD Wed). (Ben: PDF attch)
- ZenithWorks shares the security questionnaire + any network allowlist requirements (Alicia).
- Schedule a focused SDK pairing session (45m) next week to walk through function contracts and streaming client (suggest Wed/Thu morning PT).

Attachments referenced: ZenithWorks->security checklist (you mentioned bringing this to us) and our proposed MVP scope (we’ll attach).

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll follow up with the MVP doc and a proposed calendar invite.

Thanks,

Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@zenithworks.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: ZenithWorks discovery — SDK changes & infra asks

Thanks, Sergio — this is a good summary and captures the discussion well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: the p95 ~1.2s is measured at the API edge after our retrieval step; ideally the reranker contributes <400ms to stay under 1s overall.
- For the pilot we can accept hosted with VPC peering as you suggested; data residency is not a blocker for pilot but must be addressed for production.
- Security questionnaire: attaching our network/security checklist (network-security-checklist.xlsx). It includes our allowlist, TLS requirements, and a short set of audit questions.

Two asks: 
1) Can you provide any benchmark numbers for expected p95 with 8-bit quantized versus fp16 for a 1k-token rerank on an A100-equivalent backend? Even approximate ballpark numbers will help our infra team sign off.
2) Can you include an example function contract for create_ticket in the MVP doc? We want to see how validation is enforced end-to-end.

Available times for the SDK pairing session next week (PT): Wed 9:30–11:00, Thu 10:00–11:00. Prefer Wed.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Head of Product Engineering | ZenithWorks
alicia.ramos@zenithworks.com

Attachment: network-security-checklist.xlsx (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@zenithworks.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: ZenithWorks discovery — SDK changes & infra asks

Alicia — appreciate the checklist, attaching our proposed MVP scope PDF with a short cost range and the example function contract. High-level notes here so the pairing session is productive: 

1) Benchmarks (ballpark):
- fp16 (baseline) on A100-equivalent: rerank 1k-token inference p95 ~ 180–220ms (model-only, excluding network).
- 8-bit quantized (int8/llm.int8): rerank 1k-token p95 ~ 240–300ms with a ~6–9% throughput reduction vs fp16 but token cost ~40% lower in our Hosted pricing.
- Real-world p95 at your stack (including retrieval + network) we estimate reranker contribution ~300–400ms — should meet your <400ms goal if prefix caching is used and batching tuned.

2) SDK changes for pilot (JS/TS):
- streaming-client.ts: handles server-sent events and incremental token/app state mapping (approx. 180 LOC).
- func-contracts.ts: JSON Schema for create_ticket / rerank_review; server-side validator helper (approx. 120 LOC).
- adapter.ts: small shim to map function outputs to your internal event schema (lightweight).

3) Function contract example (excerpt included in attached PDF):
- create_ticket: {"type":"object","properties":{"ticket_id":{"type":"string"},"priority":{"enum":["low","med","high"]},"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["ticket_id","summary"]} 

4) Streaming & structured outputs: we recommend using function-calling for discrete ops (tickets, labels) and structured outputs (JSON Schema) for richer assistant responses to avoid brittle text parsing.

5) Embeddings/rerank: proposed pilot flow:
- nightly dense embedding index (FAISS) for candidate retrieval.
- online hybrid rerank: top-50 dense candidates -> model-based rerank for final score.

Attachments: zenith-proposed-mvp-scope.pdf (stub) — includes timeline, estimated cost buckets, and the full function contract.

Next steps I’ll take today:
- Upload the MVP PDF (attached) and drop a calendar invite for Wed 9:30 PT for the SDK pairing.
- Sergio / Kimberly to prepare the short pairing agenda: function contract walk-through, streaming demo, and integration checklist.

Ben Carter
